regions.name: British Columbia
visual_identifiers: dramatic mountains meeting coast or valleys
very dense dark green conifer forests
specific BC road sign style — white and green
Pacific coast feel in coastal areas
specific BC yellow road markings on highways

state_distinguishers.Vancouver_area: Urban density, specific BC Transit infrastructure, mountain backdrop to city
state_distinguishers.Interior_BC: Drier pine forests, Okanagan valley vineyard landscape, more arid than coast

regions.route_sign_clues: BC uses specific blue and white provincial route markers. Highway 1 (Trans-Canada) runs through BC.
regions.gemini_hint: Very dramatic mountains + dark green rainforest + Pacific feel = BC. Blue and white BC route markers are distinctive. Okanagan vineyard landscape = Interior BC.
common_false_positives: Dense conifer forests — also in Alberta and Washington State USA

regions.name: Prairie Provinces
visual_identifiers: Alberta has Rocky Mountains to the west

state_distinguishers.Alberta: Rocky Mountains visible to west, oil industry infrastructure, more prosperous feel than Saskatchewan/Manitoba, specific AB route markers
state_distinguishers.Saskatchewan: Most flat of all three, grain elevator culture, very sparse population density
state_distinguishers.Manitoba: More lakes visible, transition toward boreal forest in north, Winnipeg urban area

regions.route_sign_clues: Alberta uses AB prefix. Saskatchewan uses SK prefix. Manitoba uses MB prefix on route markers.
regions.gemini_hint: Rocky Mountains visible to west = definitely Alberta. Flattest possible terrain with grain elevators = Saskatchewan. More lakes and boreal transition = Manitoba.
common_false_positives: Flat prairie — all three provinces share this
Grain fields — common across all three
Wide straight roads — nationwide prairie feature

regions.name: Ontario and Quebec
visual_identifiers: Great Lakes coastal areas in Ontario
Canadian Shield rocky terrain in places

state_distinguishers.Quebec: French language on ALL signs — most reliable identifier. Specific Quebec blue and white route markers. Distinct Quebec architecture in rural areas.
state_distinguishers.Ontario: English signs. Specific Ontario route markers. More American-feeling infrastructure near US border.

regions.route_sign_clues: Quebec autoroutes use A prefix. Ontario uses Queen's Highway markers. Language on signs is THE most reliable identifier.
regions.gemini_hint: French on signs = Quebec, full stop. This is the most reliable provincial identifier in Canada. English only = Ontario or western provinces.
common_false_positives: Mixed forests — both provinces share this
Rocky Shield terrain — both provinces share this

regions.name: Atlantic Provinces
visual_identifiers: Acadian French culture in New Brunswick

state_distinguishers.PEI: Red soil is completely unique — most reliable identifier. Very flat island terrain. Potato farming landscape.
state_distinguishers.Newfoundland: Most distinct feel — rugged rocky coastline, specific Newfoundland vernacular architecture, very remote
state_distinguishers.Nova_Scotia: Cape Breton highlands in north, Halifax urban area in south
state_distinguishers.New_Brunswick: Bilingual French/English signs, more forested than other Maritime provinces

regions.route_sign_clues: Each province has own route markers. PEI routes are numbered simply. NB has bilingual signs.
regions.gemini_hint: Red soil = PEI almost certainly. Bilingual French/English signs = New Brunswick. Very rugged remote rocky coast = Newfoundland. French on signs = Quebec or New Brunswick.
common_false_positives: Atlantic coastal feel — hard to distinguish provinces without specific signs

regions.name: Northern Territories

state_distinguishers.Yukon: Alaska Highway runs through it, more mountainous, Whitehorse city infrastructure
state_distinguishers.NWT: Yellowknife city, Great Slave Lake nearby, specific NWT infrastructure
state_distinguishers.Nunavut: Arctic tundra, Inuit cultural infrastructure, no roads connecting communities

regions.route_sign_clues: Alaska Highway (Highway 1) through Yukon. Very few paved highways.
regions.gemini_hint: Extremely remote subarctic or arctic = northern territories. Alaska Highway signs = Yukon. Inuit cultural elements = Nunavut.
common_false_positives: Remote subarctic feel — hard to distinguish territories
